usage_notes: Factual educational in-game photo panels with visible credits, no NASA endorsement, no promotional or merchandise permission implied. NASA guidance distinguishes third-party copyright and recognizable-person publicity rights; review those restrictions before any commercial/promotional reuse. No crop or creative alteration is applied. These photographs depict ISS hardware or an Earth prototype, never an operating Mars colony.

photos.title: Radio communications aboard the ISS
photos.caption: NASA astronaut Jonny Kim uses a ham radio to speak with students from the International Space Station. This is ISS communications, not a Mars control room.
photos.creator: NASA; individual photographer not identified on the official page
photos.candidate_note: Selected the ham-radio photograph in the article, not its Cupola hero photograph or author avatar.
photos.processing: NASA-served bounded-width JPEG; full frame, no local image edits

photos.title: ISS solar arrays above Earth
photos.caption: Solar arrays on the Russian segment of the International Space Station, photographed by an Expedition 38 crew member on February 5, 2014. Earth is visible beyond the station.
photos.creator: Expedition 38 crew member; individual photographer not identified on the official page
photos.candidate_note: Replaced the appendix's ESA/NASA-credited solar-array image with this NASA-credited ISS photograph to avoid assuming NASA guidance also licenses a partner's photograph.

photos.title: Radishes in the ISS Advanced Plant Habitat
photos.caption: Radishes growing in the Plant Habitat-02 experiment aboard the International Space Station, photographed on November 11, 2020. The chamber supports controlled plant-growth research.
photos.creator: Kate Rubins
photos.candidate_note: Appendix candidate retained; the photograph shows plants and habitat equipment.
